"Three pages of pictures tell the story of the Lone Eagle's life at Lebec, Calif., where he mastered the art of gliding."
"On one of his first flights Lindbergh soared fifteen miles over the Tehachapi Mts., where the American ace mastered the technique of the new sport of motorless flying."
"Colonel Lindbergh, right, looking over the soaring country near Lebec, Calif., with W. Hawley Bowlus, America's foremost flyer of motorless airplanes."
"Lindbergh is working on a wing of the glider that cracked during an experimental flight."
"The Colonel is helping Bowlus hook up the glider controls."
"After the flying is over, the Lebec campers, with Mrs. Lindbergh [Anne Morrow Lindbergh] at the table, center, and her famous husband, left, are resting."
"Dragging the sailplane behind a car to the starting point, where runners stretched the heavy rubber cable that shot the light plane out into rising air currents at the top of a hill."
"Dr. Alexander Breese, Government weather expert, installing the anemometer and vane which showed Lindbergh direction and force of the wind so he could plot the best course."
"The great flyer is hard at work soldering a wire in assembling the engineless sailplane which he flew."
"Mrs. Lindbergh [Anne Morrow Lindbergh] is an interested observer of the experimental glider flights near Lebec."
"Lindbergh and Bowlus at work assembling the sailplane."
"Attaching shock cord to nose of Lindbergh's glider just before he took off."
